- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often fails to mean-revert; add a 1–2% downward bias to forecast if sentiment > 0.2 and price is declining.
- Model consistently overestimates short-term (1–7 day) reversals; apply 1–3% downward adjustment if true outcome shows early correction.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to over-forecast; apply 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment if sentiment is between 0.0 and 0.3.
- If true outcome is below 65.00, model often overestimates; apply 1–3% downward adjustment if price is below 65 and sentiment is weak or negative.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is strongly positive and price is rising; add 0.5–2% upward bias if sentiment > 0.4 and price is trending up.
- Forecast should be capped at 3–5% below recent 10-day high if sentiment is negative and price is falling.
